about: KOBE-387 seeded memory store for the relevance eval (fictional company Larkspur). Written before the queries; see README.md. scope: user = the runner's own in the Workspace, portable = the runner's portable preferences, team = the Workspace, site = the Site. age_days sets the version's age (recency).

items.statement: Prefers comparisons laid out as a table, one column per option, instead of bullet lists.
Write in British English spelling (colour, organise, licence).
Never use emoji in replies or in documents drafted for me.
Keep answers short: lead with the answer in one or two sentences, details only if asked.
For data analysis scripts, use Python with pandas rather than R.
Use the 24-hour clock and state the time zone (Europe/London) for times.
In SQL I share, keywords in upper case and one clause per line.
When making charts, avoid pie charts; use bar or line charts with labelled axes.
Draft emails to customers in a warm but direct tone, no more than five sentences, signed with first name only.
Prefers meetings scheduled before 11:00; afternoons are kept for focused work.
In code reviews, point out problems as numbered findings with severity, not inline prose.
Show money in GBP with the £ sign unless the source data is in another currency, then show both.
Slide decks: at most one idea per slide and no more than ten slides.
Code snippets for the terminal assume vim as the editor, not nano.
When recommending something, give the main reason and one alternative considered.
Use metric units (kilometres, kilograms, Celsius).
Call me by my first name; no formal salutations such as Dear.
Write TypeScript examples with strict types; avoid any.
Cite the source document or link for any figure quoted.
Summaries for executives avoid technical jargon and acronyms unless defined.
Weekly status summaries use three headings: Done, Next, Blocked.
Charts should use a colour-blind-safe palette.
Long answers use Markdown headings; short ones none.
Larkspur's headquarters are in Leeds; the second office is in Lisbon.
The fiscal year starts on 1 February and ends on 31 January.
Larkspur had 214 employees at the end of FY2026.
Amara Okafor is the CEO; Tomasz Wilk is the CFO.
Salaries are paid on the 25th of each month, or the previous working day.
Everyone gets 27 days of annual leave plus the public holidays of their office's country.
IT support requests go to the #it-help channel; urgent laptop problems by phone on extension 4400.
Expenses are submitted in Pleo within 30 days of the purchase.
Larkspur has a SOC 2 Type II report, renewed every October.
The data protection officer is Helena Costa; personal-data requests go to privacy@larkspur.example.
The analytics warehouse is Snowflake, account in the eu-west-1 region.
dbt models live in the larkspur-dbt repository; the production job runs at 05:00 UTC daily.
Our largest customer by contract value is Halden Freight (about £1.2M a year).
On-call paging is done through PagerDuty; the data platform rota changes every Monday at 10:00.
Company dashboards are built in Metabase at metrics.larkspur.example.
Airflow was retired in March 2026; all scheduling now runs in Dagster.
Raw event files in the landing bucket are kept for 400 days, then deleted.
Priya Raman leads the data platform team; Jonas Berg is the engineering manager.
We had 1,840 paying customer accounts at the end of Q3 FY2026.
Logo churn in Q3 FY2026 was 2.1%, up from 1.6% in Q2.
There are three plans: Starter, Growth and Enterprise; Enterprise is priced per seat with a 50-seat minimum.
The staging database is refreshed from production every Sunday night with personal data masked.
Accounts receivable days (DSO) were 48 at the end of Q3, against a target of 40.
Professional services revenue is recognised when the work is delivered, not when it is invoiced.
My manager is Jonas Berg; our one-to-one is on Thursdays.
My work laptop is a 2024 MacBook Pro with 32 GB of memory.
I am currently working on the churn prediction model for the Growth plan.
ARR (annual recurring revenue) is the annualised value of all active subscription contracts on the last day of the month; one-off services and usage overages are excluded.
MRR is ARR divided by twelve; we report it only for the Starter plan, which bills monthly.
Net revenue retention (NRR) is this month's ARR from customers who were customers twelve months ago, divided by their ARR then.
Revenue run rate in investor updates is last month's total invoiced revenue times twelve, services included.
An active user is a person who ran at least one query or opened a dashboard in the last 28 days; API-only service accounts do not count.
A customer counts as churned on the day their last subscription contract ends without renewal, not when they give notice.
A sales-qualified lead (SQL) is a lead with a booked discovery call and a company of more than 50 employees.
Customer acquisition cost is sales and marketing spend in a quarter divided by new customers won in that quarter.
A P1 incident is any outage or data loss affecting more than 10% of customers or any Enterprise customer's production use.
Gross margin excludes R&D and counts hosting, support salaries and third-party data costs as cost of revenue.
In our product a project is the customer-facing container for dashboards; internally the table is called space.
Data freshness means the age of the newest row in a model; the SLA is under 6 hours for tier-1 models.
Tier-1 dbt models are the ones that feed the board pack and the customer-facing usage page.
Time to value is the number of days from contract signature to the customer's first shared dashboard.
A seat is a named user with an editor or admin role; viewers are free and not counted as seats.
Expansion revenue is the increase in ARR from existing customers through upgrades or added seats, net of downgrades.
Stickiness is daily active users divided by monthly active users, averaged over the month.
A ticket is done when it is merged, deployed to production and the owner has checked it there.
Personal data here includes names, emails, IP addresses and device ids; hashed emails still count as personal data.
A signup cohort is all accounts created in the same calendar month (UTC).
Uptime is measured per calendar month from the external probe; planned maintenance announced 72 hours ahead is excluded.
The ARR dashboard in Metabase is owned by finance; ask Tomasz Wilk's team for access.
Branch names follow <ticket>-<short-slug>, for example DATA-412-fix-churn-join.
Commit messages use conventional commits: feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:.
dbt SQL uses lowercase keywords, CTEs instead of subqueries, and one model per file named stg_, int_ or mart_.
Every pull request needs one approving review from someone outside the author's pod before merge.
Snowflake tables are snake_case and plural; timestamps end in _at and dates in _on.
Meeting notes go in Notion under Team > Meetings, titled with the date (YYYY-MM-DD) and topic.
During an incident, open a channel named #inc-YYYYMMDD-short-name and post updates every 30 minutes.
Postmortems are blameless, written within five working days, and reviewed at the Friday ops meeting.
No production deploys after 15:00 on Fridays or during the last two days of the fiscal quarter.
Every Metabase dashboard has an owner named in its description; unowned dashboards are archived after 90 days.
Credentials live in 1Password vaults; never paste them into Slack, tickets or notebooks.
Timestamps are stored in UTC; convert to local time only in the presentation layer.
Customer-facing documents use American English; internal ones use British English.
Tickets are estimated in t-shirt sizes (S, M, L); anything bigger than L must be split.
Ad-hoc data requests from other teams come in through the Data Requests form, not direct messages.
Stand-up is asynchronous in #data-standup by 10:00 each weekday.
New product features ship behind a LaunchDarkly flag that is removed within two sprints of full rollout.
Python packages need tests for every public function; CI fails below 80% line coverage.
Figures in the board pack are rounded to one decimal place and shown in thousands of pounds.
Never name customers in public talks or blog posts without written permission from marketing.
2025-11: we chose Snowflake over BigQuery for the warehouse because of EU data residency and existing contracts.
2026-01: Dagster replaces Airflow for orchestration; new pipelines must not be written for Airflow.
2026-02: no new R code; existing R reports are ported to Python by the end of FY2027.
2026-04: we keep Metabase for internal dashboards and will not buy Looker; revisit in 2027.
2026-06: the churn model uses gradient boosted trees (XGBoost) rather than a neural network, for explainability.
2026-07: Growth plan list price rises 8% from 1 September 2026 for new customers; existing customers keep their price until renewal.
2026-03: all customer data is hosted in the EU (Frankfurt and Dublin); no US region for now.
2026-05: on-call engineers get a fixed £300 per week on rota plus time off in lieu after a night page.
2026-08: hiring is frozen for non-engineering roles until the end of Q4 FY2026.
2026-02: people work from the office at least two days a week, Tuesday and one day of their choice.
2026-09: all internal tools must use Okta single sign-on; tools without SSO are being retired.
2026-10: Kobe is the approved AI assistant; pasting customer data into other chatbots is not allowed.
2026-04: we run dbt Core in Dagster instead of paying for dbt Cloud.
2026-06: the board pack's headline retention metric is NRR, replacing logo churn.
Q4 FY2026 priority for the data team is the self-serve usage page for Enterprise customers.
2026-09: the legacy CSV export endpoint will be switched off on 31 January 2027; customers move to the API.
2026-05: event collection moves from Segment to our own Snowplow pipeline to cut cost.
2026-03: staging may only contain masked personal data; no production copies on laptops.
2026-07: application databases standardise on PostgreSQL 17.
2026-01: customer support covers 07:00-19:00 UK time on weekdays; Enterprise gets 24/7 for P1 incidents.
The Leeds office kitchen has an espresso machine on the third floor; descale it on Fridays.
Lisbon office parking spaces are booked through the Facilities app.
The cycle-to-work scheme opens for applications each April.
Set your Slack status to focus to mute non-urgent pings.
The guest Wi-Fi network is Larkspur-Guest; its password changes monthly and is shown on the reception screen.
The data team's offsite is in Porto from 12 to 14 May 2027.
The Leeds office has a lending library of business and technical books.
2026-04: new joiners get a hoodie and a notebook, no other swag.
